SPIKE COMPLETE. Findings: DATE/DATE_AND_TIME/TIME_OF_DAY have zero interpreter support today (confirmed). All three are 32-bit/uint, mirroring TIME's boxing: DATE/DT = seconds since 1970-01-01 epoch, TOD = ms since midnight (range 0..86399999). Comparison is exact equality, no delta, confirmed against upstream FB_TestSuite.TcPOU (AssertEquals_DATE/_DATE_AND_TIME/_TIME_OF_DAY all use <> with no Delta param). Scope for gd2.13 (~7-9 files, same shape as completed gd2.3 TIME/LTIME work): Token.cs (3 new token types), Lexer.cs (3 new word branches + new digit/-/:/. char-class scan loop, distinct from TIME's digit+letter loop), new DateTimeLiteral.cs (YYYY-MM-DD / HH:MM:SS[.mmm] / combined parsing -> uint), Expr.cs (3 literal Expr classes), Parser.Expressions.cs + Engine.Expressions.cs (3 case arms each), Engine.Defaults.cs (0u default), Engine.SizeOf.cs (3x size=4 entries), ScalarAssertType.cs (3 registry entries, WrapUInt-based exact compare like TIME). One open design decision for gd2.13: raw uint vs calendar-string failure-message formatting (upstream uses DATE_TO_STRING/DT_TO_STRING/TOD_TO_STRING calendar formatting, not raw numbers) - current TIME/LTIME precedent uses raw integers, gd2.13 should decide. Gotchas noted: DT has no ms precision despite uint width matching TIME; uint epoch-seconds overflows ~2106 (acceptable); TOD upper bound 86399999ms needs enforcing; single-letter D# literal prefix collision risk is same accepted pattern as existing T#/LT#. No source files modified (read-only research).

Full end-to-end DATE/DATE_AND_TIME/TIME_OF_DAY support: new DateTimeLiteral.cs parser (D#/DATE#, DT#/DATE_AND_TIME#, TOD#/TIME_OF_DAY# literals, uint representation per gd2.12 spike - epoch-seconds for DATE/DT, midnight-ms for TOD), lexer/parser/engine wiring, default values, SIZEOF entries, and 3 new ScalarAssertType registry rows (exact WrapUInt compare, no delta, raw-uint formatting per documented decision). AssertEquals_DATE/_DATE_AND_TIME/_TIME_OF_DAY work via the existing gd2.11 registry-driven dispatch with no NativeMethodBridge changes needed. Value model: keep tree-based Cell model as default. Use escape analysis - any variable with ADR(x) taken anywhere gets allocated in a real flat byte store (TwinCAT layout rules); everything else stays tree-based. Scope: address-taken locals + VAR fields first; skip globals until needed. Boundary is a hard rule: a held pointer dereferenced outside the escaped set, or arithmetic on a non-escaped variable, throws unsupported-construct at the throw site - never a silent/best-effort value (this is exactly the case the failure taxonomy exists for; a silent approximation would let TcAgent "fix" a false negative).

Fact-check during grilling: existing single-call MEMCPY/MEMSET/MEMMOVE round-trip (Engine.ByteLayout.cs) already reuses SizeOfType's alignment/pack_mode math, so it's internally consistent for named-variable-to-named-variable copies - "rebuild everything on a flat buffer" was overbroad. But internal consistency isn't TwinCAT conformance (pack and SIZEOF agree by construction, which can't catch a wrong rule) and four single-call cases likely still diverge from real TwinCAT even without escape analysis:
- interior/out-of-bounds ADR (MEMCPY past a buffer's end) - pick a policy (favor hard error over silent truncation) and document it
- partial-field writes (copy count not aligned to field boundaries) - must not silently vanish
- MEMCPY overlap on one named variable (e.g. ADR(arr[0])/ADR(arr[2]) with overlapping ranges) - pack/copy/unpack via a separate buffer accidentally gives MEMMOVE semantics; must implement true MEMCPY (overlap-incorrect) semantics
- count expressions that aren't SIZEOF of either operand

Root cause was NativeCallContext.TryGetArg (Extensibility/NativeCallContext.cs), not ArgBinder/BindParams - BindParams already binds named-then-positional calls correctly via ArgBinder.TryResolveArg. Native-function plugins pass 'position' as the parameter's declared signature index, but TryGetArg indexed straight into PositionalArgs by that raw index, so a preceding named argument made every later positional lookup miss by exactly the number of named args before it. Fixed by tracking discovered named positions per call and shifting the PositionalArgs index by how many of them precede the requested position. 3. Field naming unified: suite-level errorKind -> kind, errorConstruct -> construct. One vocabulary (kind/construct) at every JSON level - top-level error, suite-level error, per-test failure. Breaking rename from today's three-name inconsistency.

4. parse-error JSON shape pinned: kind: "parse-error". Reuses existing line/bodyLine fields for position - no new position field. The offending token (required by TcXunit-229.6's "carrying the offending token and line") is carried in the now-unified construct field rather than a new dedicated token field - one field for "the identifier/text that characterizes this failure" regardless of kind.

5. Inline agent directive, uniform across all five kinds - every message is self-contained actionable guidance an agent can act on without ever reading the README, no docs-only carve-outs:
   - assertion: fix the code under test or the expectation
   - plc-fault: real runtime defect, fix the code under test
   - unsupported-construct: STOP, escalate as a grammar gap, never rewrite the POU to make it pass (retrofit - today this guidance lives only in doc comments/README, not the message text)
   - load-error: check file/path/XML/discovery, not about the code under test (retrofit - today raw exception passthrough)
   - parse-error (new): open the cited line; fix if genuinely malformed; STOP and escalate if it looks like valid ST

6. schemaVersion field: skipped for now. Pre-1.0, no external JSON consumer yet - TcXunit.Vsix shells out to this same CLI/repo and upgrades in lockstep (see tcxunit-verify-wiring-not-doc-comments memory). Tracked as a backlog item so it isn't forgotten once a second consumer exists.

Decision recorded in the DESIGN field: (1) Latin-1 is the assumed narrow encoding, per Beckhoff's documented default, and a code point above U+00FF raises instead of silently truncating; {attribute 'TcEncoding':='UTF-8'} is a named out-of-scope gap since nothing parses pragmas. (2) Both capacity and content are byte-measured - that is a fact, not a choice - and under Latin-1 the two coincide; content lands in 2o9.6, capacity enforcement split out as 2o9.9 because the Cell carries no declared type. (3) One shared helper in the interpreter beside StringByteCell, consumed by Engine.Get/SetStringByte, ByteLayout pack/unpack, and CharacterMeasure.Narrow. Primary-sourced, and it corrected the premise: within Latin-1 one byte IS one code unit, so the narrow measure was already right and 2o9.6 rescoped from 'make it byte-counted' to 'guard the range and unify the paths'. Two beads filed from what surfaced: 2o9.8 (WSTRING sized n+1, TwinCAT says 2*(n+1), wrong alignment too) and 2o9.9 (STRING(n) capacity unenforced).
